item.title: Work on new Numuru bridge in Madang progressing well
item.description: Construction work on the new Numuru bridge is progressing well, according to the Department of Works and Highways in Madang. Construction workers began launching the new bridge across the river on Wednesday after successfully assembling it early this week.
item.content:encoded:
Construction work on the new Numuru bridge is progressing well, according to the Department of Works and Highways in Madang.

Construction workers began launching the new bridge across the river on Wednesday after successfully assembling it early this week.

They completed the process yesterday morning and have moved onto the next phase of installing decks and then, work on the footings.

The Numuru bridge collapsed last month under a heavy load of gravel that was on route to Bogia for similar civil works.

The bridge is likely to be ready for use in a week's time.

NBC News was on site yesterday and witnessed the completion of the bridge launching.

Locals we spoke to expressed gratitude to the government and the Department of Works and Highways for fast- tracking the construction of the new bridge.

Commuters are currently still using a bamboo footbridge and boats to cross over the river at a fee of K2.00 per person whilst charges for cargoes vary, depending on the loads.

Buai buyers and sellers are equally happy with the progress of reconstruction, stating the past weeks have been challenging for them as they continue to pay K10 for a bag of betelnut to be ferried across the river.

Meanwhile, wet- crossing on the beach front is no longer possible as it trespasses a conservation area, and locals were charging a hundred kina per vehicle.

item.title: Grade 12 exam disrupted by armed intruders in Wewak
item.description: Grade 12 examinations at Bishop Leo secondary school in Wewak were disrupted today after a group of intruders allegedly entered an examination room and attacked students and invigilators. NBC News was reliably informed by school staff that the security breach occurred while Grade 12 students were sitting for their Mathematics Examination Paper 2.
item.content:encoded:
Grade 12 examinations at Bishop Leo secondary school in Wewak were disrupted today after a group of intruders allegedly entered an examination room and attacked students and invigilators.

NBC News was reliably informed by school staff that the security breach occurred while Grade 12 students were sitting for their Mathematics Examination Paper 2.

According to the information received, the intruders were allegedly armed with guns and wire catapults and damaged examination papers during the incident.

One male student was reportedly injured after being struck by a projectile from a wire catapult and was taken to Boram hospital for medical attention.

Police are now on the ground assessing the situation.

Following the incident, students have protested to the Provincial Education Division over the security breach, while police continue to monitor the situation.

Further details are expected as authorities establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

item.title: Lae businesses still struggle with power blackouts
item.description: The commissioning of a new transmission line is a step towards improving electricity reliability in Lae, but businesses and residents continue to face prolonged blackouts and rising operating costs. Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry president John Byrne says reliable electricity is essential for the city, Papua New Guinea’s main manufacturing, distribution, transport and logistics hub.
item.content:encoded:
The commissioning of a new transmission line is a step towards improving electricity reliability in Lae, but businesses and residents continue to face prolonged blackouts and rising operating costs.

Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry president John Byrne says reliable electricity is essential for the city, Papua New Guinea’s main manufacturing, distribution, transport and logistics hub.

“The commissioning of the new transmission line is a positive step for reliable power for Lae City and is vital for redundancy and supply of power,” Byrne said.

However, he said electricity supply to businesses and communities remained poor, with the impact of El Niño on water levels at Yonki Dam contributing to load-shedding.

Combined with existing supply problems, this has resulted in prolonged blackouts and power spikes.

Businesses are increasingly relying on diesel generators to keep operating, adding to costs as fuel prices rise.

Byrne said electricity disruptions were also affecting water services, raising concerns about public health, hygiene and the risk of disease.

He welcomed efforts by the PNG Power board and management, the Government and other stakeholders to restore a more reliable and affordable electricity supply.

“While we cannot control the weather or El Niño, these challenges are not being ignored,” he said.

“A country without power is a powerless country, and we must resolve this issue.”

Byrne said reliable electricity was critical to Lae’s economy and its role in supplying goods and services to communities across the country.

He said the new transmission line was an important step, but sustained efforts were needed to address the wider power supply problems affecting businesses and residents.

item.title: NDC supports North Fly drought response
item.description: Member for North Fly James Donald has thanked the National Disaster Centre for its timely support in coordinating logistics and hiring a landing craft to freight 120 tons of food relief supplies to affected communities in North Fly District of Western Province. Donald utilized District Services Improvement Program funds and internal revenue to purchase 500 tons of immediate relief supplies, mainly
item.content:encoded:
Member for North Fly James Donald has thanked the National Disaster Centre for its timely support in coordinating logistics and hiring a landing craft to freight 120 tons of food relief supplies to affected communities in North Fly District of Western Province.

Donald utilized District Services Improvement Program funds and internal revenue to purchase 500 tons of immediate relief supplies, mainly food and other dry goods and water, for communities affected by the El Nino-induced drought.

The National Government responded promptly through the NDC, which arranged transport to move the first 120 tons to Aiambak for distribution.

Further support is also being provided by partners, with the Australian Government to airlift 10 tons of supplies to Tabubil, while Ok Tedi Mining Limited will airlift a further 50 tons to Tabubil.

In a statement, Donald said getting relief into remote parts of North Fly is a major challenge especially during this drought when the Fly River water level has decreased, and the NDC's help with logistics has made a real difference for their people.

Acting Director General of the NDC, Laso Mana said the NDC is committed to supporting provincial and district leaders to get help to drought-affected communities as quickly as possible, and this operation shows what can be achieved when National Government, district leadership, development partners and the private sector work together.

The NDC continues to monitor drought conditions in North Fly and across the country and is coordinating with provincial and district authorities on further assistance.

As operator, EMPNGA will work closely with the Government of Papua New Guinea, the Gulf and Central Provincial Governments, local communi
item.content:encoded:
Exxon Mobil PNG Antelope Limited (EMPNGA), an affiliate of Exxon Mobil Corporation, has formally assumed operatorship of the Papua LNG Project following an agreement reached by the project’s co-venturers TotalEnergies, Santos, and ENEOS Xplora in September 2026.

As operator, EMPNGA will work closely with the Government of Papua New Guinea, the Gulf and Central Provincial Governments, local communities, and project co-venturers to advance the project safely, responsibly, and efficiently.

The co-venturers remain focused on progressing the project toward a final investment decision (FID) later this year.

“Amidst global uncertainty Papua New Guinea continues to be an attractive investment destination for investors. The success of the ExxonMobil PNG-operated PNG LNG Project demonstrated what PNG can deliver, with the Papua LNG Project set to further strengthen the country’s position in the global energy landscape.” said Dinesh Sivasamboo, Chairman and Managing Director of EMPNGA.

“We are honored to assume operatorship of the Project and appreciate the confidence placed in ExxonMobil by our co-venturers, the Government of Papua New Guinea, and the Gulf and Central Provincial Governments."

“Also, we thank TotalEnergies for their efforts to progress the Project and look forward to working together with all stakeholders toward a final investment decision and helping advance Papua New Guinea’s next chapter of LNG development,” he said.

EMPNGA has collaborated closely with all levels of government and the Papua LNG co-venturers to progress the Project.

The operatorship transfer builds on ExxonMobil’s longstanding presence in Papua New Guinea and leverages the company’s experience in LNG development and operations, creating opportunities for collaboration with the ExxonMobil PNG-operated PNG LNG Project.

Papua LNG is expected to support Papua New Guinea’s long-term economic development by creating jobs during construction, supporting local businesses and generating benefits for communities across the country.

The Project is a key part of the government’s economic vision that will, along with the intended development of the P’nyang LNG Project after Papua LNG as well as resources such as Muruk and Wildebeest, see over a decade of investment in the country.

item.title: Boroko Motors technicians to represent PNG in Japan
item.description: Papua New Guinea will have two representatives at one of Isuzu’s major international technical competitions in Japan two weeks from now. Boroko Motors technicians Stephen Vai and Allan Kobua were selected to represent PNG at the 2026 Isuzu Grand Prix Competition where they will join competitors from 36 countries.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea will have two representatives at one of Isuzu’s major international technical competitions in Japan two weeks from now.

Boroko Motors technicians Stephen Vai and Allan Kobua were selected to represent PNG at the 2026 Isuzu Grand Prix Competition where they will join competitors from 36 countries.

They will be brining their technical expertise and diagnostic skills to an event that recognises excellence in automotive servicing and technical problem-solving.

The competition will challenge participants over two days (Oct 27-28), beginning with virtual fault diagnosis before progressing to practical technical examinations.

Both stages will require a strong understanding of vehicle systems, accurate fault identification and the ability to apply technical knowledge under competitive conditions.

Vai and Kobua earned their places following a nationwide selection process involving Boroko Motors locations in Port Moresby, Lae, Mount Hagen, Goroka, Kokopo, Madang and Tabubil.

They advanced through multiple assessment stages to secure the opportunity to represent their company and country on the international stage.

Their achievement reflects the importance of continuous learning and professional development within the automotive industry.

Boroko Motors, under the leadership of General Manager Liza Marie Brooks, has continued to invest in developing its people and strengthening the technical capabilities of its national workforce.

A key part of this commitment is the BM Training Academy, established approximately one year ago and led by Head of National Training and Technical Support Manoj J.

The Academy supports employee development through technical training, diagnostic capability building and structured learning opportunities designed to improve performance across the company’s operations.

Coach Otto Wouda will accompany both technicians to Japan, providing support as they prepare for the demands of the competition.

Participation in the event will also expose the technicians to international practices, different diagnostic approaches and technical standards used across other markets.

The knowledge and experience gained will provide an opportunity to share new learning with colleagues, strengthen technical capability within Boroko Motors and contribute to improved service quality for customers throughout PNG.

For Stephen and Allan, the competition represents an opportunity to demonstrate their individual skills while contributing to the wider recognition of PNG’s automotive workforce.

Their participation also highlights the potential of national employees when supported through training, practical experience and opportunities for professional advancement.

Boroko Motors remains committed to developing capable national employees who can meet evolving industry requirements and contribute to the country’s future.

Their participation in Japan is an important milestone in that commitment and an opportunity to showcase PNG’s talent before an international audience.

item.title: Aitape wharf redevelopment expected to revive regional trade
item.description: The redevelopment of Aitape Wharf is expected to restore an important maritime link for trade, business and the movement of essential goods in the middle Sepik area. The National Government has officially launched the redevelopment project, which is expected to strengthen Aitape's role as a transport and commercial centre for coastal and inland communities
item.content:encoded:
The redevelopment of Aitape Wharf is expected to restore an important maritime link for trade, business and the movement of essential goods in the middle Sepik area.

The National Government has officially launched the redevelopment project, which is expected to strengthen Aitape's role as a transport and commercial centre for coastal and inland communities

The project is expected to restore the wharf's capacity to handle cargo and support the movement of goods and passengers, following the collapse of its main structure in February 2021.

Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso, who officiated at the launch, described the redevelopment as a government priority. “Your Member (Anderson Mise) has been fighting for this project. Once it is complete, Aitape will thrive as an economical hub for this part of the country,” Rosso said.

Built in 1972 and refurbished in 1990, Aitape Wharf played an important role in connecting communities to markets and essential supplies. Its operations supported local businesses and helped facilitate the movement of goods between Aitape and other centres.

The loss of the wharf has created challenges for cargo transportation, with goods now having to travel by road between Aitape and Wewak. The journey can take approximately three to five hours each way, while flooding at river crossings can further disrupt road transport.

Moreover, the economic potential of the redevelopment extends beyond the wharf itself. PNG Ports Corporation estimates that the redeveloped facility could handle approximately 25,000 tonnes of cargo annually and support around K101 million in regional economic activity each year.

These projections highlight the potential contribution of the port to trade and business. However, the K101 million figure represents estimated regional economic activity associated with the facility, and not the gross domestic product of Aitape town.

Improved maritime transport could provide better opportunities for farmers, fishermen, traders and other local producers to move their products to markets.

Aitape-Lumi MP Anderson Mise has been involved in efforts to progress the redevelopment, which is expected to provide long-term benefits for the district.

“We are connecting our farmers to markets, we are connecting our fisherman to buyers, we are connecting the people. The district will benefit from this,” said Mise.

The planned works include a new main wharf and mooring structure, rehabilitation of the access trestle and small-ship wharf, and the installation of new equipment to support vessel docking.

The project is being funded through PNG Ports Corporation, at the cost of K22-K25million with China Harbour Engineering Company as the contractor.

Minister for State-Owned Enterprises William Duma has called on the people of Aitape-Lumi to take an active interest in the project and its implementation.

The redevelopment is expected to take 12 months, although the construction commencement and completion dates should be confirmed by the relevant authorities.

For Aitape, the project represents an opportunity to restore a key piece of transport infrastructure and strengthen the town's connection to regional trade.

item.title: UOG students question reduced HELP loan allocations
item.description: University of Goroka students are demanding answers from the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (DHERST) over HELP loan payments that fall short of the amounts they applied for. University of Goroka Student Representative Council (SRC) President Justin Muna and students presented a petition to DHERST yesterday, raising concerns over reduced loan payments and whether t
item.content:encoded:
University of Goroka students are demanding answers from the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (DHERST) over HELP loan payments that fall short of the amounts they applied for.

University of Goroka Student Representative Council (SRC) President Justin Muna and students presented a petition to DHERST yesterday, raising concerns over reduced loan payments and whether the funds would adequately cover their education costs.

The Higher Education Loan Programe (HELP) is a government initiative designed to ease the cost of tertiary education by providing financial assistance to students.

The student leader raised concerns over discrepancies between the loan amounts students expected to receive and the payments reflected in DHERST’s records.

“The amounts students received did not match what they applied for, or the amounts shown in online records after vetting,” he said.

Muna added that while online records showed some students were expected to receive up to eight thousand kina, a few received as little as fifty-three kina, raising concerns over discrepancies between the approved loan amounts and actual payments.

The SRC president revealed that HELP loans were approved for one thousand six hundred and forty-two students, with a total of about Seven million kina expected to be disbursed. However, he raised concerns that the amount reflected in DHERST’s payment list was significantly lower.

“We were not satisfied with the further verbal explanations provided by DHERST officials, prompting us to submit a petition through the university’s Pro Vice-Chancellor Academic to demand clear answers and warn of further action if our concerns remain unresolved,” Muna said.

The UOG students have requested a response from DHERST by October 15, as stated in their petition.
